title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: modules over a base ring k, the divided-power functors Γ^n, and for a module A the functor F_A(X) = Hom(A,X). The next page writes this as Hom_1(A,X): linear maps, i.e. polynomial laws of degree 1.

(1) Universal divided powers. u_n : A → Γ^n(A), a ↦ a^{[n]}, is the universal homogeneous polynomial law of degree n (Roby). Normalisation: u_0 = 1, u_1 = id. For f : A → X, Grothendieck defines the divided powers of f as f^{(n)} := Γ^n(f) ∘ u_n : A → Γ^n(X). This is a degree-n polynomial law, i.e. an element of F_A(Γ^n X) in the polynomial sense. f ↦ f^{(n)} is itself homogeneous of degree n, so it induces a map Γ^n(F_A(X)) → F_A(Γ^n X). This is what the top line 'Γ^{pq}(F_A(X)) → F_A(Γ^{pq}(X))' records. The next page asks for exactly such natural maps β : Γ^n F(X) → F(Γ^n X) for a general functor F.

(2) Composition axiom without numerical coefficients. σ^X_{pq} : Γ^{pq}(X) → Γ^p(Γ^q(X)) is the natural map coming from the wreath product S_q ≀ S_p ⊂ S_{pq} on invariant tensors. It sends x^{[pq]} to (x^{[q]})^{[p]}.
- Universal case (X = A, f = id, circled diagram): σ^A_{pq} ∘ u_{pq} = Γ^p(u_q) ∘ u_p.
- General f: naturality of σ gives Γ^p(Γ^q f ∘ u_q) ∘ u_p = Γ^pΓ^q(f) ∘ Γ^p(u_q) ∘ u_p = Γ^pΓ^q(f) ∘ σ^A ∘ u_{pq} = σ^X ∘ Γ^{pq}(f) ∘ u_{pq}.
- That is, (f^{(q)})^{(p)} = F_A(σ^X_{pq})(f^{(pq)}).
This is the PD axiom (x^{[q]})^{[p]} = (pq)!/(p!(q!)^p) x^{[pq]}, stated functorially through σ instead of the integer coefficient.

(3) Product axiom. The quadratic diagonal Δ : A → A⊗A, x ↦ x⊗x, followed by u_p⊗u_q and the multiplication γ_{p,q} : Γ^p⊗Γ^q → Γ^{p+q}, gives C(p+q,q)·u_{p+q}. The boxed identity u_p·u_q = C(p+q,q) u_{p+q} is read in the graded algebra Hom_•(A, Γ*A) of polynomial laws. The partly illegible text says this algebra is graded and that its product comes from a 'coalgebra structure' on A (the diagonal) and the algebra structure of Γ*A. The next page abstracts this: a functor F with bilinear pairings F_A(X)×F_B(Y) → F_C(X⊗Y) yields a diagonal A → A⊗A, whose coassociativity, cocommutativity and counit correspond to associativity, commutativity and unit.

Purpose. The page belongs to the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex. It seems to aim at a functorial, coefficient-free notion of a 'functor with divided powers' (F with maps Γ^n F → F Γ^n satisfying σ- and γ-compatibilities). The representable functor Hom(A,-), with divided powers coming from the universal laws u_n, is the model case.
errors: On the second line the label σ^X_{pq} is put on the map Γ^{pq}(F_A(X)) → F_A(Γ^{pq}X). That map is really f ↦ f^{(pq)} = Γ^{pq}(f)∘u_{pq}; σ^X_{pq} : Γ^{pq}X → Γ^pΓ^qX enters only after F_A is applied. This is notational looseness in scratch notes, not a mathematical error.
u_n is not linear, so f^{(n)} lies in degree-n polynomial laws, not in Hom_1(A,Γ^n X). The page tacitly treats 'Hom' as the graded space of polynomial laws Hom_•. No real gap, just unstated.

ideas.what: Divided powers of a linear map defined by f^{(n)} = Γ^n(f)∘u_n using the universal degree-n polynomial law u_n : A → Γ^n A
ideas.modern_name: universal polynomial laws / divided powers of maps (Roby); strict polynomial functor formalism
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963-65); Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for strict polynomial functors

ideas.what: PD composition axiom stated as compatibility with the natural transformation σ_{pq}: Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q (wreath-product inclusion) instead of the coefficient (pq)!/(p!(q!)^p)
ideas.modern_name: plethystic / monadic description of divided power structures (Γ as a comonad-like structure; Γ(P,-) for operads)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; B. Fresse (2000) for operadic divided power algebras

ideas.what: u_p·u_q = C(p+q,q) u_{p+q} in the graded algebra of polynomial laws A → Γ*A, the product induced by the diagonal and the multiplication of Γ*A
ideas.modern_name: convolution product on polynomial laws; divided-power algebra relation

ideas.what: Abstracting functors with bilinear pairings F_A×F_B → F_C(⊗) to recover a (co)algebra structure on the representing object

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a coefficient-free axiomatics for 'functors with divided powers' F (maps Γ^nF → FΓ^n compatible with σ_{pq} and γ_{p,q}), taking Hom(A,-) as the model case. This appears to be groundwork for a functorial treatment of the PD de Rham complex. Similar ideas exist later (Fresse's Γ(P,-), strict polynomial functors), but this particular formulation is a modest unpublished thread with no clear published continuation by him.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it shows Grothendieck around 1976 treating divided powers via natural transformations between the Γ-functors, anticipating the operadic/polynomial-functor viewpoint. It contains no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are standard divided-power identities. The only mildly notable feature is the functorial, coefficient-free formulation via σ_{pq}, which anticipates later polynomial-functor and operadic viewpoints but is not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Top crossed-out line reads '[-F_A(Γ^{pq}(X))-]' followed by '→ Γ^{pq}(f)∘u_{pq}'. The second line's source is Γ^{pq}(F_A(X)), not F^{pq}.
'f^{(pq)} ∈' on the left, with 'f^{Γ}' under F_A(X), likely means the element f^{(pq)} attached to f ∈ F_A(X).
'Tor_1(A, Γ*A)' should read 'Hom_•(A, Γ*A)' (graded space of polynomial laws), consistent with 'Hom_1' on the next page. The right side is plausibly 'Hom_•(S·Ǎ ..., ...)' and is uncertain.
'ds' = 'dans'. The lines below are probably 'qui est une alg. gr. grâce à la structure de cog. sur A et la structure d'alg. de Γ*A'.
Label under A → Γ^{p+q}(A) is 'C(p+q,q) u_{p+q}'.
'k{T}' is probably a marginal note on the divided-power polynomial algebra in one variable.
